title: janhq/jan — Jan is an open source alternative to ChatGPT that runs 100% offline on your computer.
content:
Getting Started - Community - Changelog - Bug reports
Jan is bringing the best of open-source AI in an easy-to-use product. Download and run LLMs with full control and privacy.
The easiest way to get started is by downloading one of the following versions for your respective operating system:
Download from jan.ai or GitHub Releases.
- Local AI Models: Download and run LLMs (Llama, Gemma, Qwen, GPT-oss etc.) from HuggingFace
- Cloud Integration: Connect to GPT models via OpenAI, Claude models via Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, MiniMax, and others
- Custom Assistants: Create specialized AI assistants for your tasks
- OpenAI-Compatible API: Local server at localhost:1337 for other applications
- Model Context Protocol: MCP integration for agentic capabilities
- Privacy First: Everything runs locally when you want it to
For those who enjoy the scenic route:
- Node.js ≥ 20.0.0
- Yarn ≥ 4.5.3
- Make ≥ 3.81
- Rust (for Tauri)
- (macOS Apple Silicon only) MetalToolchain xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain
git clone https://github.com/janhq/jan
cd jan
make dev
This handles everything: installs dependencies, builds core components, and launches the app.
Available make targets:
- make dev - Full development setup and launch
- make build - Production build
- make test - Run tests and linting
- make clean - Delete everything and start fresh
yarn install
yarn build
yarn dev
Minimum specs for a decent experience:
- macOS: 13.6+ (8GB RAM for 3B models, 16GB for 7B, 32GB for 13B)
- Windows: 10+ with GPU support for NVIDIA/AMD/Intel Arc
- Linux: Most distributions work, GPU acceleration available
For detailed compatibility, check our installation guides.
If things go sideways:
- Check our troubleshooting docs
- Copy your error logs and system specs
- Ask for help in our Discord #🆘|jan-help channel
Contributions welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full spiel.
- Documentation - The manual you should read
- API Reference - For the technically inclined
- Changelog - What we broke and fixed
- Discord - Where the community lives
- Bugs: GitHub Issues
- Business: hello@jan.ai
- Jobs: hr@jan.ai
- General Discussion: Discord
Apache 2.0 - Because sharing is caring.
Built on the shoulders of giants:

report.summary: Jan is an open-source, offline ChatGPT alternative for running LLMs locally with privacy, cloud integrations, and custom assistants.
report.background: The rise of ChatGPT popularized conversational AI but raised concerns about data privacy, vendor lock-in, and recurring subscription costs. Open-source LLMs like Llama, Gemma, and Qwen have matured enough to run on consumer hardware, yet installing and managing them remains technical. Jan fills this gap by wrapping these models in a polished, easy-to-use desktop app built with Tauri. It offers a ChatGPT-like interface that runs entirely on-device, giving users full control over their data. Additionally, Jan bridges local and cloud AI: users can switch to hosted models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, or MiniMax when local hardware is insufficient. This hybrid approach appeals to privacy-conscious individuals, developers prototyping AI features, and organizations wanting to avoid sending sensitive data to third-party APIs. Jan is Apache 2.0 licensed, leveraging the open-source ecosystem and community contributions to accelerate development.
key_points: Jan runs 100% offline, downloading models like Llama, Gemma, Qwen, and GPT-oss from HuggingFace directly onto your machine. This ensures data never leaves your computer, providing maximum privacy and independence from cloud services or subscription fees.

It includes cloud integration, letting you connect to GPT via OpenAI, Claude via Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, MiniMax, and more. This flexibility lets users combine local speed and privacy with cloud-scale models when needed, all from one interface.

Users can create custom assistants tailored to specific tasks, similar to ChatGPT's custom GPTs. This makes it easier to build specialized tools for writing, coding, research, or personal productivity without needing deep programming knowledge.

Jan provides an OpenAI-compatible API server at localhost:1337, allowing other applications to interact with local models seamlessly. This dramatically lowers the barrier for developers who want to experiment with open-source LLMs using familiar tooling and libraries.

The app supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling agentic capabilities by connecting models to external tools and data sources. This positions Jan as a serious platform for building autonomous AI workflows rather than just a chat client.

System requirements scale with model size: 8GB RAM is fine for 3B models, while 13B models need 32GB. GPU acceleration works on Windows with NVIDIA/AMD/Intel Arc and Linux, making high-performance local AI accessible to many users with modern hardware.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Jan demonstrates that open-source models can be packaged into consumer-friendly products that rival proprietary assistants, accelerating the shift toward decentralized AI. Developers gain a free, local alternative for testing prompts and building prototypes without cloud costs or rate limits, plus an OpenAI-compatible API that reuses existing code. Regular users benefit from privacy and no monthly fees, but they must invest in capable hardware and accept that smaller models are less capable than frontier AI. Jan's MCP support also hints at a future where personal AI agents run entirely on-device, raising questions about how cloud providers will differentiate as local inference improves.
report.tools: Watch Jan's GitHub repository (janhq/jan) for releases and roadmap. Pair it with Ollama for lightweight local model management, LM Studio for another GUI option, and HuggingFace Hub to browse downloadable models. For developers, explore the OpenAI Python SDK against Jan's localhost:1337 server, and study Tauri if you want to build similar cross-platform desktop AI apps.
